stem.en: A workshop has a lump of brass and wants the copper and the zinc back as separate metals. The workshop has a filter, a magnet and a separating funnel. What can it do with these?

text.en: Nothing. Brass is an alloy, the same all the way through, so none of these has anything to work on.
Filter it after grinding, because the zinc grains are smaller than the copper grains.
Use the magnet, because zinc is attracted and copper is not.
Melt it and use the funnel, because the copper will form a lower layer.

explanation.en: Brass is a homogeneous mixture, so grinding only gives smaller bits of the same brass, each with both metals in it. Neither copper nor zinc is attracted by a magnet. Melted brass is one liquid, not two layers, so a funnel has nothing to release. Copper really is denser than zinc, which makes the funnel idea reasonable, but the two metals stay mixed in the melt.

hints.en: Is brass the same all the way through?
For each tool, ask what it would need to find in the brass.
